title: Rezonings for housing towers and Trussler Road
subtitle: Bird Friendly City certification, heritage designations, dog designation ruling, Conrad Centre operating model and hospital lease assignment.
overview: Council approved several zoning changes that will add housing. These were a townhouse development at 60 Trussler Road, a revised high-rise at 864-876 King Street West, and a project at 169-183 Victoria Street South. The Trussler Road vote was split {{vote:m3}}. Councillors who supported it said the planning case was sound and that a refusal would likely be overturned on appeal. Those opposed wanted the developer to show more flexibility.

Council also endorsed Kitchener becoming a Bird Friendly City certified by Nature Canada. It approved a heritage permit for an addition at 115 Lancaster Street East and started the process to designate five more properties as heritage sites. It ratified a decision to re-designate a dog as Prohibited rather than Dangerous.

Council also approved a new operating model for the Conrad Centre for the Performing Arts, extended advisory committee terms, and adopted new corporate policies. After a closed session, it authorized a lease assignment for the Grand River Hospital lands, a land acquisition and a land disposition at 59 Bedford Road. The mayor noted that city and regional budget consultations are under way, and the city's public consultation is the following Monday evening.

decisions.detail: Council approved the zoning change for 60 Trussler Road on a recorded vote {{vote:m3}}, following staff's recommendation.
Council approved amended zoning for King Pine Kitchener Inc., allowing slightly larger floor plates and reduced tower separation from the north property lines, and waived further notice.
Council approved zoning changes under both by-laws and endorsed the Urban Design Brief for the site, with the new zoning taking effect only once the Growing Together by-law is in force.
Council approved partial demolition, a three-storey addition and alterations to the building, subject to heritage conditions.
Council endorsed Nature Canada Bird Friendly certification and agreed to mark World Migratory Bird Day each year on the second Saturday of May.
Council ratified the appeal committee's decision to replace the Dangerous Dog designation with a Prohibited Dog designation.

Council approved the operating model subject to the 2025 budget, authorized a mentorship agreement with Green Light Arts until June 30, 2026, and delegated rental approvals to the Director of Culture & Entertainment.
Council authorized assigning the lease for the hospital lands at 835 King Street West to the new hospital, subject to the Ministry of Health's satisfaction.

debate: On Trussler Road, some councillors were disappointed that the developer did not attend as requested and that no visual barrier, unit reduction or three-bedroom units were added. Staff said a barrier could not be required beyond what the by-law specifies, and that provincial changes limit council's say over building design at site plan.

Councillors who supported Trussler Road said it met planning rules and that refusal would likely go to the Ontario Land Tribunal, which they said usually sides with developers. Opponents wanted to send developers a message about working with councils and communities.

On King Street West, the developer's team said an error required shifting the tower about one metre closer to the school sports field. Staff said they had no concerns because that yard is undevelopable open space. Councillors welcomed the three-bedroom units and asked about community use of the field.

On Victoria Street South, one councillor opposed the rezoning, citing traffic from many projects in the area, piecemeal planning, loss of existing rental homes and a lack of separation from the heritage district. Staff said the rental replacement by-law applies, traffic studies include approved projects, and the site fits the planned function of the area.

On the Lancaster Street heritage permit, a resident delegate argued the addition sits in a front or side yard, which conflicts with the heritage district plan. Staff said that under the zoning by-law definitions the addition is in the rear yard and is subordinate and appropriate. The applicant said the addition would pay for extensive repairs.
